DWG bow-string junction (Smith, PASP): outgoing waves = incoming + rho_hat(v_d+)*v_d+, with rho_hat = r/(1+r), r = 0.25*R_b(v_d)/R_s; for R_b >= 0, rho_hat lies in [0,1), so the junction is passive; nut reflects velocity waves with sign inversion; losses/dispersion are lumped into reflection filters.

claim: With the DAFx26 loss model (eq. 2), mode n of a string of vibrating length Lv decays at sigma_n = s0 + s1*(n*pi/Lv)^2, so T60_n = 3 ln10 / sigma_n; for the yehu F4 string (Lv=0.295 m) T60 = 5.44 s (n=1), 1.21 s (n=4), 0.23 s (n=10). Values in S-06 OUTPUT.json serve as a decay oracle.

Plucking in DWG can be modelled as a structurally passive scattering junction (finger/plectrum compliance as a spring, optional nonlinear 'feathering' compliance), which guarantees stability independent of the excitation; earlier balanced finger/pick perturbation (Eckerholm & Evangelista 2008) and plectrum modelling (Germain & Evangelista, WASPAA 2009, 25-28) exist.

The yehudafx26 reference code (commit 284e5be2) differs from the DAFx26 paper's Table 1: rho 1300 for both strings (paper 1250/1350), f0 344/513 Hz (paper F4/C5), sigma0 string 2 = 1.5884 (paper 1.5844), bridge 0.08 m from the stub giving a 0.30 m vibrating length. The code additionally provides 11 bridge modes (M,K,R) and a 25-section parallel radiation filter designed at 44.1 kHz, not tabulated in the paper. Plan uses paper values for strings and code values only for body/radiation (S-07).
